study_context.outcome: Major cardiovascular events (nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, cardiovascular death)
study_context.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk

Younger adults with type 2 diabetes (bas.hypothesis: Younger adults with type 2 diabetes (baseline age < 50 years) benefit more from intensive glycemic control because longer remaining lifespan provides more opportunity for reduction in atherosclerotic progression and fewer competing risks from hypoglycemia.

In adults with type 2 diabetes and high.hypothesis: In adults with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, participants with BMI >= 35 kg/m^2 will experience less reduction in major cardiovascular events from intensive glycemic control (target HbA1c <6.0%) compared with participants with BMI < 35 kg/m^2.

Among adults with baseline HbA1c >= 8.0%.hypothesis: Among adults with baseline HbA1c >= 8.0%, intensive glycemic control (target HbA1c <6.0%) will provide little or no reduction in major cardiovascular events compared with standard glycemic control.

subgroup_rule.description: baseline HbA1c greater than or equal to 8.0%

Adults with type 2 diabetes duration <=.hypothesis: Adults with type 2 diabetes duration <= 5 years will experience greater reduction in major cardiovascular events with intensive glycemic control (target HbA1c <6.0%) compared with those with longer diabetes duration.

subgroup_rule.description: Diabetes duration of five years or less

In adults with type 2 diabetes and high.hypothesis: In adults with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥150 mmHg predicts a reduced benefit from intensive glycemic control (target HbA1c <6.0%) versus usual glycemic control for preventing major cardiovascular events.

subgroup_rule.description: Baseline systolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 150 mmHg
